name: chat.scheduleMessage
purpose: Schedules a message to be sent to a channel.

as_user.desc: Set to true to post the message as the authed user, instead of as a bot. Defaults to false. Cannot be used by new Slack apps. See chat.postMessage.

attachments.desc: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string.

blocks.desc: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string.

channel.desc: Channel, private group, or DM channel to send message to. Can be an encoded ID, or a name. See below for more details.

link_names.desc: Find and link user groups. No longer supports linking individual users; use syntax shown in Mentioning Users instead.

markdown_text.desc: Accepts message text formatted in markdown. This argument should not be used in conjunction with blocks or text. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.

parse.desc: Change how messages are treated. See chat.postMessage.

post_at.desc: Unix timestamp representing the future time the message should post to Slack.

reply_broadcast.desc: Used in conjunction with thread_ts and indicates whether reply should be made visible to everyone in the channel or conversation. Defaults to false.

text.desc: How this field works and whether it is required depends on other fields you use in your API call. See below for more detail.

thread_ts.desc: Provide another message's ts value to make this message a reply. Avoid using a reply's ts value; use its parent instead.

unfurl_links.desc: Pass true to enable unfurling of primarily text-based content.

unfurl_media.desc: Pass false to disable unfurling of media content.

metadata.desc: JSON object with event_type and event_payload fields, presented as a URL-encoded string. Metadata you post to Slack is accessible to any app or user who is a member of that workspace.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
